verdicts.claim: SQLite triggers passive checkpoints automatically when the WAL hits a configurable threshold (defaulting to 1,000 pages) or when connections close
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes' (overview is uncited; checked against c1-1)

verdicts.claim: SQLite checkpointing copies committed database pages from the write-ahead log (-wal) file back to the primary database file, allowing the log
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file'; writer rewinds WAL once fully checkpointed

verdicts.claim: By default, SQLite automatically executes a passive checkpoint whenever a write transaction commit expands the WAL file to 1,000 pages or more
verdicts.evidence: wal.html sec 3.1 1000-page COMMIT threshold; 'All checkpoints initiated ... by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'

verdicts.claim: SQLite provides sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 with modes PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE to programmatically control blocking behavior
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: FULL/RESTART 'can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()', names SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE; primary c3ref/wal_checkpoint_v2.html confirms TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes' (also lists NOOP)

verdicts.claim: Litestream holds an intentional indefinite read transaction on SQLite to pause automatic checkpointing
verdicts.evidence: litestream.io: 'It starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file' (source says long-running, not indefinite)

verdicts.claim: ...while it copies WAL frames into an external shadow log for continuous replication
verdicts.evidence: litestream.io mentions 'a directory of shadow WAL files' only as the older-release design, saying v0.5 replaces it with TXID-based LTX files; c1-2 URL 404s; present-tense claim likely outdated

verdicts.claim: Passive checkpoints cannot advance past frames pinned by active readers, causing WAL file growth and potential starvation
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader' and 'the WAL file will grow without bound'

notes: Draft holds only ~7 distinct load-bearing claims (one concept), so sampled=7, not 10.
